parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘covert sensitisation’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Outline how the aversive stimulus was used in the study by Glover (2011) to treat the woman’s
kleptomania.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Give two differences between covert sensitisation and imaginal desensitisation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using covert sensitisation to treat impulse
control disorders. You should include a conclusion in your answer. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

text: A woman was treated by Glover (2011) for kleptomania. She had a 14-year history of daily
compulsive shoplifting and was treated with covert sensitisation. At a 19-month follow-up she was
free of stealing behaviour apart from one lapse, and there were corresponding improvements in
her self-esteem and socialisation.

parts.label: (c)

Suggest how one model of the ‘effects of ambience’ explains how perceived crowding can
make the ambience of a shop less pleasant.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of using questionnaires to investigate the effect of
crowding when shopping in a retail store. You should include a conclusion in your answer. 
Psychology and health

text: Machleit et al. (2000) found that perceived crowding in shops, created by manipulating either
human (social) density or spatial density, changed levels of pleasure and satisfaction.

parts.text: Suggest why the Funhaler™ is a ‘behavioural technique’ to improve adherence.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Suggest two reasons why children may not adhere and therefore fail to take prescribed
medication.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of conducting studies on non-adherence in
children. You should include a conclusion in your answer. 
Psychology and organisations

text: The consequences of irregular treatment and poor inhalation technique for children with asthma
are linked to more hospitalisations and increased morbidity. The ‘Funhaler’™ is a novel spacer
device for asthma, devised by Watt et al. (2003) which aims to improve adherence.

Psychology and abnormality

text: When goal-setting, some organisations set workers targets and some organisations do not.
‘Even though little Hans was just one child, the psychoanalytic explanation of phobias can be
generalised to everyone.’
To what extent do you agree with this statement? Use examples of research you have studied to
support your answer. [12]
